}}"The Reason" is a song by American rock band Hoobastank. Released on January 26, 2004, as the second single from their second studio album of the same name, the power ballad is Hoobastank's most commercially successful single, peaking at number two on the US Billboard Hot 100 and number one on the US Modern Rock Tracks chart. In 2005, it was nominated for two categories at the 47th Annual Grammy Awards: Song of the Year and Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals. Internationally, "The Reason" reached number one in Bolivia, Canada, Ecuador, and Italy while peaking within the top 10 in 13 additional countries.

sections.heading: Background and release
sections.wikitext:
Following Hoobastank's tour in support of their 2001 [[Hoobastank (album)|self-titled debut album]], the band began writing songs again for a follow-up album. Upon playing the opening riff of "The Reason", guitarist Dan Estrin began to flesh out the song and sent a completed instrumental demo to lead singer Douglas Robb. Using pieces of old lyrics and stream-of-thought ideas written in his journal, Robb quickly constructed the song's lyrics.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Houghton |first=Cillea |date=December 1, 2023 |title=Interview: Hoobastank's Dan Estrin on "The Reason": "It's a Very Relatable Sentiment" |url=https://americansongwriter.com/interview-hoobastanks-dan-estrin-on-the-reason-its-a-very-relatable-sentiment/ |access-date=September 14, 2024 |website=[[American Songwriter]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=France |first=Lisa |date=December 4, 2023 |title=Hoobastank has 'The Reason' to celebrate |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/12/04/entertainment/hoobastank-reason-20th-anniversary/index.html |access-date=September 14, 2024 |website=[[CNN]]}}</ref>

"The Reason" was first released as part of the band's second studio album ''[[The Reason (Hoobastank album)|The Reason]]'' on December 9, 2003. Robb noted how "[[Out of Control (Hoobastank song)|Out of Control]]" was chosen as the album's first single due to its more [[Heavy rock|heavy]] sound, despite their record label's insistence that "The Reason" be released.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Lipshutz |first=Jason |date=December 7, 2023 |title=20 Questions: Hoobastank Celebrates 20 Years of 'The Reason' |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/hoobastank-the-reason-20th-anniversary-interview-1235544552/ |access-date=September 14, 2024 |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Houghton |first=Cillea |date=December 11, 2023 |title=Interview: Hoobastank on "The Reason" Anniversary Show: "We're All Really Excited" |url=https://americansongwriter.com/interview-hoobastank-on-the-reason-anniversary-show-were-all-really-excited/ |access-date=September 14, 2024 |website=[[American Songwriter]]}}</ref> However, the band eventually decided to release the song as a single, and it was serviced to radio stations starting January 26, 2004.<ref name=":1" />
sections.text:
Following Hoobastank's tour in support of their 2001 self-titled debut album, the band began writing songs again for a follow-up album. Upon playing the opening riff of "The Reason", guitarist Dan Estrin began to flesh out the song and sent a completed instrumental demo to lead singer Douglas Robb. Using pieces of old lyrics and stream-of-thought ideas written in his journal, Robb quickly constructed the song's lyrics.

"The Reason" was first released as part of the band's second studio album The Reason on December 9, 2003. Robb noted how "Out of Control" was chosen as the album's first single due to its more heavy sound, despite their record label's insistence that "The Reason" be released. However, the band eventually decided to release the song as a single, and it was serviced to radio stations starting January 26, 2004.

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
On March 20, 2004, the song debuted on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] at number 62, becoming that week's "Hot Shot Debut".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/2004-03-20?rank=62|title=The Hot 100 – Week of March 20, 2004|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=December 2, 2020}}</ref> It reached its peak of number two after 13 more weeks on the listing, giving the band their highest-charting US single. Though it remained on the chart for 38 issues, it was their last Hot 100 hit.<ref name="hot100"/> The single peaked atop the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Adult Pop Airplay|Adult Top 40]], [[Alternative Airplay|Modern Rock Tracks]], and [[Pop Airplay|Mainstream Top 40]] charts.<ref name="usaps"/><ref name="usas"/><ref name="usps"/> In Canada, it topped ''[[Radio & Records]]''{{'}} CHR/Pop, Hot AC, and Rock charts.<ref name="can"/><ref name="canhac"/><ref name="canrock"/> The song was a radio hit in Central and South America, topping the airplay charts of Bolivia and Ecuador and peaking at number three in El Salvador.<ref name="bol"/><ref name="ecu"/><ref name="els"/>

In Europe, "The Reason" reached number one on the [[Italian Singles Chart]] and the [[UK Rock & Metal Singles and Albums Charts|UK Rock & Metal Singles Chart]] for two weeks each.<ref name="ita"/><ref name="ukr"/> On the [[UK Singles Chart]], it debuted and peaked at number 12, while on the [[Scottish Singles Chart]], it entered the top 10, peaking at number six.<ref name="uk"/><ref name="scot"/> Across the rest of Europe, the track entered the top 10 in Austria,<ref name="aut"/> the Czech Republic,<ref name="czr"/> Greece,<ref name="gre"/> Latvia,<ref name="lat"/> the Netherlands,<ref name="d40"/> Norway,<ref name="nor"/> Sweden,<ref name="swe"/> Switzerland,<ref name="swi"/> and [[Wallonia]].<ref name="wal"/> It was also successful in Oceania, reaching number seven in Australia and number five in New Zealand.<ref name="aus"/><ref name="nz"/>
sections.text:
On March 20, 2004, the song debuted on the US Billboard Hot 100 at number 62, becoming that week's "Hot Shot Debut". It reached its peak of number two after 13 more weeks on the listing, giving the band their highest-charting US single. Though it remained on the chart for 38 issues, it was their last Hot 100 hit. The single peaked atop the Billboard Adult Top 40, Modern Rock Tracks, and Mainstream Top 40 charts. In Canada, it topped Radio & Records{{'}} CHR/Pop, Hot AC, and Rock charts. The song was a radio hit in Central and South America, topping the airplay charts of Bolivia and Ecuador and peaking at number three in El Salvador.

In Europe, "The Reason" reached number one on the Italian Singles Chart and the UK Rock & Metal Singles Chart for two weeks each. On the UK Singles Chart, it debuted and peaked at number 12, while on the Scottish Singles Chart, it entered the top 10, peaking at number six. Across the rest of Europe, the track entered the top 10 in Austria, the Czech Republic, Greece, Latvia, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland, and Wallonia. It was also successful in Oceania, reaching number seven in Australia and number five in New Zealand.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
The music video for the song was directed by [[Brett Simon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/1485805/hoobastank-heist-pawn-shop-in-dark-new-video-expound-upon-life-philosophy/|title=Hoobastank Heist Pawn Shop In Dark New Video; Expound upon Life Philosophy|last=Wiederhorn|first=Jon|publisher=[[MTV]]|date=March 17, 2004|access-date=January 10, 2021}}{{dead link|date=June 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> In it, the band members stage a diversion so they can carry out the elaborate theft of "The Chiara Ruby #2" gem from a [[pawnshop]], but those facts are only clear after enough of the action unfolds: nothing is as it seems. At the beginning of the video, a woman (played by Serbian model Nevena Milicevic)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www-biografija-org.translate.goog/moda/nevena-milicevic/?_x_tr_sl=auto&_x_tr_tl=en&_x_tr_hl=en-US&_x_tr_pto=wapp|title=Nevena Milicevic|website=Biografija.org|date=January 31, 2022 |access-date=July 29, 2023}}</ref> gets hit by a car driven by vocalist Doug Robb. After the "accident", while everyone's attention is diverted, Chris Hesse and Dan Estrin execute the heist. The viewer then realizes that she was in on the operation, as she gets up and rides off with an accomplice on a motorcycle at the end. The presumed owner of the pawnshop displays a look of realization, and the song ends with the band admiring their new acquisition, holding it up to the light and projecting red light-rays onto the ceiling. The accident's "victim" is also present. They then hear police sirens from above, and the video fades out.

Their music video "[[Same Direction]]" is intended as both a sequel and a prequel to the video for "The Reason" and further details the band members' roles, as well as showing the trouble they bring down on themselves from law enforcement.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/1488675/new-hoobastank-video-picks-up-where-the-reason-left-off/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160331051046/http://www.mtv.com/news/1488675/new-hoobastank-video-picks-up-where-the-reason-left-off/|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 31, 2016|title=New Hoobastank Video Picks Up Where 'The Reason' Left Off|last=Vineyard|first=Jennifer|publisher=[[MTV]]|date=June 24, 2004|access-date=June 6, 2020}}</ref> On August 21, 2023, the music video reached one billion views on [[YouTube]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fV4DiAyExN0|title=Hoobastank – The Reason (Official Music Video)|date=October 7, 2009 |publisher=[[YouTube]]|access-date=August 21, 2023}}</ref>
sections.text:
The music video for the song was directed by Brett Simon. In it, the band members stage a diversion so they can carry out the elaborate theft of "The Chiara Ruby #2" gem from a pawnshop, but those facts are only clear after enough of the action unfolds: nothing is as it seems. At the beginning of the video, a woman (played by Serbian model Nevena Milicevic) gets hit by a car driven by vocalist Doug Robb. After the "accident", while everyone's attention is diverted, Chris Hesse and Dan Estrin execute the heist. The viewer then realizes that she was in on the operation, as she gets up and rides off with an accomplice on a motorcycle at the end. The presumed owner of the pawnshop displays a look of realization, and the song ends with the band admiring their new acquisition, holding it up to the light and projecting red light-rays onto the ceiling. The accident's "victim" is also present. They then hear police sirens from above, and the video fades out.

Their music video "Same Direction" is intended as both a sequel and a prequel to the video for "The Reason" and further details the band members' roles, as well as showing the trouble they bring down on themselves from law enforcement. On August 21, 2023, the music video reached one billion views on YouTube.

sections.heading: 2021 TikTok trend
sections.wikitext: In February 2021, the song became the subject of a [[Viral phenomenon|viral trend]] on the app [[TikTok]], where users, under the [[hashtag]] "#NotAPerfectPerson", would post videos featuring the song alongside text describing their embarrassing moments and personal flaws. Ellise Shafer of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' suggested that the song's sudden resurgence was due to a combination of nostalgia and the song's lyrical relatability.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shafer |first=Ellise |date=February 4, 2021 |title=Hoobastank Delighted by TikTok Popularity as 'The Reason' Goes Viral, Signaling Resurgence of '00s Hits |url=https://variety.com/2021/music/news/hoobastank-the-reason-tiktok-resurgence-00s-hits-1234899602/ |access-date=September 13, 2024 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref> As a result of the trend, Hoobastank created a TikTok account, with lead singer Doug Robb partaking in the challenge by making fun of the band's nonsensical name.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Aniftos |first=Raina |date=February 9, 2021 |title=Hoobastank's 'The Reason' Is Soundtracking Your Most Embarrassing Moments on TikTok |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/hoobastank-the-reason-viral-tiktok-9524064/ |access-date=September 13, 2024 |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Brodsky |first=Rachel |date=February 16, 2021 |title=Hoobastank's Doug Robb On Newfound TikTok Fame, Making Peace With "The Reason," And More |url=https://www.stereogum.com/2116330/hoobastank-doug-robb-tiktok-the-reason/interviews/tracking-down/ |access-date=September 13, 2024 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>
sections.text: In February 2021, the song became the subject of a viral trend on the app TikTok, where users, under the hashtag "#NotAPerfectPerson", would post videos featuring the song alongside text describing their embarrassing moments and personal flaws. Ellise Shafer of Variety suggested that the song's sudden resurgence was due to a combination of nostalgia and the song's lyrical relatability. As a result of the trend, Hoobastank created a TikTok account, with lead singer Doug Robb partaking in the challenge by making fun of the band's nonsensical name.

sections.heading: Usage in media
sections.wikitext: "The Reason" has been included in various television episodes. On May 6, 2004, the song appeared in "[[friends season 10#Specials|The One Before the Last One]]", a special episode of the sitcom ''[[Friends]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=D'Angelo |first=Joe |date=May 28, 2004 |title=And The Reason Is ... ? Hoobastank Singer's Not So Sure |url=https://www.mtv.com/news/ukekf5/and-the-reason-is-hoobastank-singers-not-so-sure |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220820060230/https://www.mtv.com/news/ukekf5/and-the-reason-is-hoobastank-singers-not-so-sure |archive-date=August 20, 2022 |access-date=September 13, 2024 |website=[[MTV News]]}}</ref> The song later appeared on the first episode of the 2023 [[Netflix]] show ''[[Beef (TV series)|Beef]]'', with lead actor [[Steven Yeun]] saying that the band was a "perfect analogy" for the show's theme of "excavating the cringe of our childhood".<ref name=":0" /> "The Reason" was also covered in the second season of the British sitcom ''[[We Are Lady Parts]]'', with creator [[Nida Manzoor]] opting to cover the song instead of writing an original one.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goffe |first=Nadira |date=May 30, 2024 |title=How ''We Are Lady Parts'' Took the Music Even Further in Season 2 |url=https://slate.com/culture/2024/05/we-are-lady-parts-season-2-peacock-nida-manzoor-band-music.html |access-date=September 13, 2024 |website=[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]]}}</ref>
sections.text: "The Reason" has been included in various television episodes. On May 6, 2004, the song appeared in "The One Before the Last One", a special episode of the sitcom Friends. The song later appeared on the first episode of the 2023 Netflix show Beef, with lead actor Steven Yeun saying that the band was a "perfect analogy" for the show's theme of "excavating the cringe of our childhood". "The Reason" was also covered in the second season of the British sitcom We Are Lady Parts, with creator Nida Manzoor opting to cover the song instead of writing an original one.
